svg.title: How scenario choices shape CANOE transportation
svg.desc: Scenario-wide period, demand, cost, efficiency and emissions settings sit above three panels. The fleet panel shows how sales and survival become calibrated vintage and powertrain cohorts, with two definitions of existing capacity. The vehicle panel shows where source-class weights combine into CANOE classes and where plug-in ranges are combined or kept separate. The charging panel traces surviving battery-electric vehicles to port counts, rated capacity, charger archetypes and their annual or hourly operation.
svg.text: How scenario choices shape CANOE transportation
From source evidence to fleet vintages, vehicle technologies and charging infrastructure

g.text: Period timing and demand
Prospective → closing · Legacy → opening
Cars follow GDP or historical growth. With historical
growth, light trucks balance combined demand.
Exchange rates and trajectories
Select CER demand and currency cases separately.
Choose ATB efficiency and cost paths separately.
Advanced · Mid · Conservative
Calibration and embodied emissions
Optional CEUD fuel fit · fixed lifetimes and flat use
GREET vehicle-cycle emissions on or off.
LDV materials can be conventional or lightweight.
Fleet vintages and powertrains
Build the historical fleet
CEUD sales + survival → annual cohorts
Fit surviving stock to CEUD class totals.
Split cohorts by powertrain
StatCan new registrations give LDV shares.
StatCan fleet counts give truck shares.
Roll cohorts into model vintages
MTO stock supplies bus and motorcycle ages.
Set lifetimes and existing capacity
EPA MOVES or NHTSA CAFE + EIA NEMS.
One source informs both medians and survival.
Fixed lifetimes
Temoa starts from physical survivors.
A vintage retires at its fixed age.
Survival curves
Temoa starts from acquisition-equivalent stock.
The surviving fraction changes with age.
Surviving BEVs → charger sizing
Vehicle classes and plug-in ranges
Combine source classes
NRCan ratings and ATB sizes → CEUD LDVs
Compact/midsize cars · SUV/pickup light trucks
ATB uses MTO size weights. Ratings use matched
MTO stock and iZEV incentive records.
ATB weight classes → CEUD medium trucks
MTO or Wards set weight-class shares. Eligible
freight vocations count equally within each class.
ATB Class 8 → CEUD heavy trucks
StatCan tonne-km weight regional day cabs and
long-haul sleepers by province.
Reuse fleet weights across parameters
ATB efficiency, costs and diagnostic VKT.
LDV weights also combine NHTSA curves.
Resolve electric range by fleet stage
Existing · One BEV and one PHEV per class.
EPA OMEGA range mix weights parameters.
New · Unconstrained, OMEGA minimum
shares by class and powertrain, or combine
ranges into weighted representatives.
Potential fleet-weight sources · SAAQ and ICBC
Charger types and operating hours
Size the existing port stock
Surviving BEVs ÷ EVs per port → total ports.
LDV total ports − observed public → private ports.
Port counts × rated power → installed GW.
Group ports into charger technologies
Aggregated
L1, L2 and DC fast → pooled LDV.
Overnight, fast and ultrafast → pooled truck.
Pooled cost/GW and annual use (20% / 30%).
Explicit
Public L2, public DC fast and private L1/L2.
Truck overnight and fast (includes ultrafast).
GW-based mix · type costs and annual factors.
Hourly profiles · pooled LDV only
NHTS (US) or TTS (Ontario) travel → RAMP.
Uncontrolled, night or day. Profiles can be off.
RAMP uses legacy sales-weighted batteries by
BEV size, independent of the range setting.
Hourly factors average 20%. Explicit types use
annual factors pending type-specific profiles.
